Content creators have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video game since its launch
Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI became the largest video game release of all time last week and while it is hard to say exactly how many people are playing the game (current estimates say at least 30 million), there are plenty of other jaw-dropping data points we do know.
Data on streaming the game suggests that only two days into its release a cumulative 364.5m hours have been watched – roughly 41,000 years of content. Put another way, that translates to more than 41,000 years worth of people riffling through cash registers, hanging drywall, birding, diving or hijacking jets. That’s according to streaming data from Streams Charts, a data and analytics company that has been tracking Rockstar Game’s long-awaited title.

articles.title: GTA in Istanbul? Meet the game developers bringing virtual crime chaos to their home cities
articles.summary:
From Helsinki to Istanbul, independent developers are putting Grand Theft Auto-style action on their home streets, and without billion-dollar budgets. They tell us how they do it
Like most kids who shouldn’t have been playing Grand Theft Auto III in 2001, Eamonn Swayah imagined a version of Rockstar Games’ groundbreaking criminal sandbox set in his own back yard. In his case, that was a Manchester council estate, complete with local accents, driving on the left, and plenty of ways to hustle.
He didn’t know it, but swapping the game’s facsimile of early 2000s New York City for a different setting was an idea he shared with many watchful game developers. Rockstar’s 3D open world template, it turned out, could be plonked in just about any location, so long as it had people and enough cars to run them over with. After GTA III attracted immense commercial success (and controversy), dozens of copycats and spiritual sequels hit the market throughout the 00s and 2010s. Gamers had a pithy name for them: “GTA clones”.

articles.title: The Cutthroat Business of Shipwrecks
Dressmaker review – delightful business sim is a cut above
articles.summary:
PC; Cosy Lives/Free Lives
Catering to the exacting whims of a small town preparing for some grand visitors presents absorbing, beautifully designed – and surprisingly thrilling – challenges

The small town of Twillford is abuzz with intrigue and excitement. A local duke has died and ladies of a certain standing are determined to make an impression at the funeral. As a newly arrived dressmaker with the only clothing shop in the area, you’re about to get plenty of work.
Thus begins this utterly delightful sim game, in which you talk to customers, gather their style preferences and tailor specific outfits just for them. It could be a suitably respectful funeral frock, with just a hint of style to catch the eye of the duke’s wealthy relatives, or perhaps a work outfit for a farmer who loves bright colours. Once you have your brief, you open your sketchbook and draft a pattern using fabric swatches and a pencil to colour in your design. Need something elegant? How about a strapless bodice. An outfit for the office? A pencil skirt is a good call.

articles.title: Slow internet? The best wifi extenders and mesh systems to boost your home network – tested
articles.summary:
We put 11 range extenders and mesh systems to the test to find the fastest and most reliable for streaming, gaming and working from home
• The best office chairs
Fast fibre broadband is fantastic – if the wifi signal reaches the part of your home where you need it. Most of us use the router provided by our broadband provider, often tucked away in a hallway or corner of the lounge. Sadly, these often don’t have the range to cover every room in your home, leaving you high and dry when you’re trying to binge-watch TV or get work done in a distant home office.
Wifi extenders and mesh systems can help. Extenders plug in to a mains socket between your location and the router, then pass data backwards and forwards to extend your router’s reach. Mesh systems are even smarter, pairing a secondary router with one or two satellite units, which work together to extend the wifi coverage throughout your home. The mesh system can pass your connection from unit to unit to make sure you’re always getting the best possible link from your device to the internet, wherever you are in your home.
